summary: In ansible-core 2.19, conditionals whose input is not a string or whose result is not a boolean are treated as errors instead of relying on truthy evaluation; ALLOW_BROKEN_CONDITIONALS temporarily downgrades this to a warning.
questions: Why does my when/assert now fail with 'Conditionals must have a boolean result'?
How can I temporarily allow non-boolean conditionals after upgrading?
Does Ansible still accept truthy values in when clauses?

answer_card.title: Broken conditionals are errors in ansible-core 2.19
answer_card.answer_md:
A conditional is "broken" when the expression isn't a string or its result isn't a boolean. Older versions silently used Python/Jinja truthiness, which hid logic errors.

ansible-core 2.19 detects non-boolean conditionals and **raises an error by default**. As a temporary measure you can downgrade it to a warning with the `ALLOW_BROKEN_CONDITIONALS` config setting, but the real fix is to make each condition return an explicit boolean.
